name: preference_op
description: Create or delete a customer preference (an alias or an event -- call list_preferences for the current list). There is no update: to change one, delete it and create a new one. Confirm with the customer before creating anything you inferred rather than that they explicitly asked for -- a bad create is just deleted, but don't silently invent preferences. Create an alias when the customer says something like 'when I say X, I mean Y' (X -> alias, Y -> target, a real device/scene/group name). Create an event for a dated fact they want tracked (birthday, anniversary, etc.) -- 'annual' repeats every year on month/day (e.g. a yahrtzeit), 'once' is a single date. remind_days_before is optional and only records the reminder intent -- no notification is actually sent (no delivery channel exists yet), but list_preferences will flag it as due_soon once it's within that window.

type.description: Required for create. Not needed for delete -- id alone is enough, ids are unique across every preference.

id.description: Required for delete, as returned by list_preferences or by a prior create. Omit for create.

alias.description: type == 'alias', create only. The customer's shorthand, e.g. 'mbr'.

target.description: type == 'alias', create only. What the alias resolves to -- a real device/scene/group name.

name.description: type == 'event', create only. Human name for the event, e.g. "Dad's yahrtzeit".

recurrence.description: type == 'event', create only. 'annual' repeats every year on month/day; 'once' is a single date.

remind_days_before.description: type == 'event', create only, optional. If set, list_preferences flags the event as due_soon starting this many days before it occurs. No notification is actually sent.
